stories.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
stories.abstract: CISA has added critical vulnerabilities in Collabora Online's Built-in CODE Server and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Both flaws are currently being leveraged by attackers in the wild to compromise exposed systems.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow for OS command injection and SQL injection, granting attackers potential full control over affected infrastructure.
stories.action: Patch Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator immediately.

stories.title: Arista Networks security advisory (AV26-1080) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities are currently being exploited in the wild across Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator, Siemens Software Center, and Gitea. CISA has added several of these flaws, including CVE-2026-114625, CVE-2026-110936, and CVE-2026-60004, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or remote code execution in enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update Arista VCO, Siemens Software Center, and Gitea to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: PHP2Shell Exploit Attempts Hit Millions as Attackers Try to Deploy Mirai Malware
stories.abstract: Two critical use-after-free vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are currently being targeted by threat actors. While initial exploitation attempts to integrate systems into the Potassium botnet have struggled, the flaws allow for unauthenticated remote code execution.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities carry a high CVSS score and pose a significant risk of remote code execution on widely deployed web infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest PHP security patches immediately.

stories.title: Quest Diagnostics warns of potential data theft after attack on lab service system
stories.abstract: Quest Diagnostics reported a security incident involving unauthorized access to its Quanum Laboratory Services Manager system. The breach potentially exposed sensitive patient information, marking another significant compromise within the healthcare technology sector.
stories.why: Healthcare providers remain high-value targets for data exfiltration, posing ongoing risks to patient privacy and regulatory compliance.

stories.title: Siemens Software Center
stories.abstract: Siemens Software Center versions prior to 4.0.9.8 contain a vulnerability where the application insecurely loads dynamic-link libraries. An authenticated local attacker could exploit this uncontrolled search path to execute arbitrary code with the application's elevated privileges.
stories.why: This flaw allows local privilege escalation, posing a significant risk to industrial and critical infrastructure environments where Siemens software is deployed.
stories.action: Update Siemens Software Center to version 4.0.9.8 or later.

stories.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
stories.abstract: Arista confirmed active exploitation of a critical SQL injection vulnerability within its VeloCloud Orchestrator. The flaw enables authenticated users, including those with restricted read-only access, to escalate privileges to the operator level and compromise the central SD-WAN management system.
stories.why: This represents the third zero-day in four months for this platform, indicating a sustained targeting of critical network management infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the security patches provided in the Arista advisory immediately.

stories.title: BlackX UEFI Bootkit Bypasses Secure Boot on Patched Windows Systems Missing Revocations
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor, likely APT41, is deploying the BlackX UEFI bootkit against diplomatic targets in Central Asia. The malware leverages the Baton Drop vulnerability to circumvent Secure Boot, allowing it to disable security software from Kaspersky and Avast at the firmware level.
stories.why: Firmware-level persistence allows attackers to maintain stealthy, long-term access that survives operating system reinstalls and evades traditional endpoint detection.

stories.title: Fortinet security advisory (AV26-1081)
Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW
stories.abstract: Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW and its Station Access Controller are affected by numerous critical vulnerabilities, including SQL injection, heap overflows, and memory corruption. These flaws could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, escalate privileges, steal credentials, or trigger denial-of-service conditions.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical infrastructure management software, potentially granting attackers full control over industrial network access and configuration.
stories.action: Update Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW and Station Access Controller to version 6.0 or later.

stories.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
stories.abstract: A memory corruption vulnerability in Google's Brotli compression library allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via maliciously crafted data. The flaw, CVE-2026-111497, impacts various runtimes and applications, including Node.js, Bun, and several Python packages that utilize the affected decoder.
stories.why: This is a critical supply chain risk, as the vulnerable library is embedded in widely used infrastructure, proxies, and language runtimes.
stories.action: Update Node.js, Bun, and Brotli-related dependencies to patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Active Exploitation of May 2026 PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20)
stories.abstract: Ransomware groups, specifically Qilin and Inc, are actively leveraging the PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 to compromise systems. This flaw, originally disclosed in May, is now seeing widespread exploitation by threat actors for malicious operations.
stories.why: The vulnerability is being actively weaponized by major ransomware syndicates, significantly increasing the risk of data encryption and extortion for unpatched Palo Alto environments.
stories.action: Apply the latest PAN-OS security patches immediately.

stories.title: HPE security advisory (AV26-1079)
stories.abstract: HPE has released security updates for ArubaOS to address 72 vulnerabilities, including eight critical flaws involving authentication bypass and remote code execution. The patches affect various versions of AOS-10 and AOS-8 networking operating systems.
stories.why: Critical vulnerabilities in network infrastructure allow attackers to bypass authentication or execute arbitrary code, potentially leading to full system compromise.
stories.action: Update ArubaOS to the latest versions specified in HPE security bulletin HPESBNW05162.

stories.title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
stories.abstract: Capcom disclosed a security incident involving its CAPCOM ID membership platform. Unauthorized actors accessed the system, compromising the personal data and email addresses of approximately 11.7 million users.
stories.why: Large-scale credential and PII exposure increases the risk of targeted phishing campaigns and account takeover attacks against the gaming community.

stories.title: Shaking in my cyber boots... #cybersecurity #ai #technews
stories.abstract: The provided source material consists solely of promotional links and social media handles for a podcast series titled The Low Down. It contains no news, security vulnerabilities, or actionable intelligence regarding the cybersecurity landscape.

stories.title: Atlassian security advisory (AV26-1076)
stories.abstract: Atlassian released a major security bulletin addressing 75 vulnerabilities across its Data Center and Server product lines, including Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye, and Jira. Many of these flaws originate from third-party dependencies, with 14 identified as critical severity.
stories.why: Unpatched Atlassian products are frequent targets for exploitation, and critical vulnerabilities in third-party components can provide attackers with unauthorized system access.
stories.action: Review the October bulletin and update all affected Atlassian products to the latest patched versions.

stories.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
stories.abstract: Security researchers from Eye Security silently pushed over two million unauthorized updates to abandoned Time4Popcorn installations. The intervention disabled a vulnerable background updater that could have allowed remote attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on affected systems.
stories.why: It highlights the risks of abandoned software and the controversial precedent of security firms performing unauthorized remote remediation on third-party devices.

stories.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
stories.abstract: A leaked master key for LiteLLM's agent platform, exposed in a public GitHub repository, enabled unauthorized access to the project's infrastructure. Attackers leveraged this credential to compromise the release pipeline and distribute a malicious version of the Python package to unsuspecting users.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks via compromised CI/CD pipelines remain a critical risk for developers relying on third-party open-source libraries.
stories.action: Audit and rotate any credentials or API keys associated with LiteLLM deployments immediately.

stories.title: (Reliable)? php2shell exploitability, (Fri, Oct 23rd)
stories.abstract: Security researchers are investigating a reported vulnerability dubbed php2shell. While initial reports triggered significant industry concern, technical details regarding the exploit's mechanics and actual impact remain unverified and sparse at this time.
stories.why: Unverified reports of remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP environments require immediate monitoring to determine if active exploitation is occurring.

stories.title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Risk Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
stories.abstract: PHP developers identified a new remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-115560, shortly after patching the critical PHP2Shell flaws. While the maintainers consider this latest risk unlikely for most standard configurations, they advise disabling the specific feature involved rather than issuing an emergency patch.
stories.why: Unpatched RCE vulnerabilities in the PHP runtime pose significant risks to server integrity, even if the current exploit vector requires specific, non-standard configurations.
stories.action: Disable the vulnerable feature as recommended in the official PHP security advisory.

stories.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Used New Mesh Network Backdoor in Destructive Ukraine Attack
stories.abstract: Sandworm and UAC-0099 collaborated on a destructive wiper attack against a Ukrainian logistics firm. The operation began with a spear-phishing campaign that delivered a custom backdoor, facilitating network infiltration and subsequent data destruction within the target environment.
stories.why: This highlights evolving TTPs where state-sponsored groups leverage mesh network backdoors to maintain persistence and execute destructive payloads in critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in the Python Pillow library allows remote code execution. By exploiting improper input validation when processing EPS files, attackers can inject malicious commands that are subsequently executed by the underlying Ghostscript utility.
stories.why: Pillow is a ubiquitous dependency; this flaw enables server-side command injection if an application processes untrusted image uploads.
stories.action: Update Pillow to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Someone Tried to Exploit PHP2Shell 4 Days Before the Vulnerabilities Were Publicly Disclosed
stories.abstract: Threat actors initiated large-scale exploitation of two critical PHP vulnerabilities four days prior to the official release of security patches. Both Amazon and Cloudflare have confirmed widespread malicious activity targeting these flaws across the internet.
stories.why: The window between vulnerability disclosure and patching was exploited, indicating attackers likely reverse-engineered the fix or utilized leaked information to target unpatched systems.
stories.action: Update all PHP installations to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
stories.abstract: The PHP project released security updates for versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to address two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities. Public proof-of-concept exploits are circulating, suggesting active exploitation. A third, less severe RCE vulnerability was also disclosed but requires specific, non-standard configurations.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in core language runtimes present a high risk for server compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Update PHP to versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 immediately.

stories.title: MongoDB security advisory (AV26-1078)
stories.abstract: MongoDB has disclosed two vulnerabilities in its C# Driver versions prior to 3.13.0, including a memory-exhaustion denial of service flaw and an authentication bypass issue involving certificate validation. Additionally, Roundcube released security updates for versions 1.6.20 and 1.7.5 to address undisclosed vulnerabilities.
stories.why: These flaws could allow attackers to crash services or bypass authentication mechanisms, posing significant risks to database and webmail infrastructure integrity.
stories.action: Update MongoDB C# Driver to 3.13.0 and Roundcube Webmail to 1.6.20 or 1.7.5.

stories.title: PHP Vulnerability Wrap-Up, (Fri, Oct 23rd)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center has downgraded the threat level to Green following recent PHP security concerns. The situation is now considered stable, and administrators should return to standard operational procedures.
stories.why: PHP vulnerabilities frequently serve as primary vectors for web-based exploitation and remote code execution.

stories.title: Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder firmware versions prior to 1.30 allow attackers to achieve full device compromise. Flaws include OS command injection, path traversal, hard-coded credentials, and missing authentication for sensitive functions.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities provide remote attackers with complete control over network-connected video hardware, potentially facilitating lateral movement or unauthorized surveillance.
stories.action: Update Kiloview E3 firmware to version 1.30 or later immediately.

stories.title: InterSystems Corporation InterSystems IRIS for Health
stories.abstract: InterSystems IRIS for Health versions 2026.2.0.221, 2026.1.0.235, and 2025.3.0.226 contain a vulnerability where TLS/SSL encryption is disabled by default. This flaw allows unauthorized parties to intercept sensitive data in transit and potentially hijack user sessions to gain unauthorized device access.
stories.why: Cleartext transmission of sensitive data exposes authentication credentials and proprietary information to interception by local or network-based attackers.
stories.action: Enable TLS/SSL encryption for all InterSystems IRIS for Health instances immediately.

stories.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
stories.abstract: Russian-speaking ransomware affiliates from the INC and The Gentlemen groups are utilizing an AI-powered framework called Phantom. This automated system streamlines the intrusion process, facilitating both unauthorized network access and subsequent data extortion activities.
stories.why: The integration of AI agents into the ransomware kill chain significantly lowers the barrier to entry for complex, multi-stage cyberattacks.

stories.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability affecting roughly 70 percent of PHP-based websites is currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw allows unauthorized actors to gain complete control over vulnerable servers, leading to widespread service disruptions as administrators rush to apply necessary patches.
stories.why: Unpatched PHP servers are prime targets for remote code execution, potentially leading to full system compromise and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Update PHP to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
stories.abstract: Certificate authority eMudhra is exiting the global SSL/TLS market following the discovery that eight of its intermediate CA private keys were cryptographically weak and easily guessable. The firm is currently coordinating with partners to replace impacted certificates for its customers.
stories.why: Compromised intermediate CA keys allow attackers to forge valid certificates, undermining the trust model for encrypted communications and potentially enabling large-scale interception.
stories.action: Revoke and replace any certificates issued by the affected eMudhra intermediate CAs.

stories.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
stories.abstract: Researchers leveraged artificial intelligence to identify long-standing security flaws within the PHP programming language. Following these discoveries, automated exploitation attempts targeting these specific vulnerabilities have emerged, demonstrating how AI lowers the barrier for attackers to weaponize legacy codebases.
stories.why: AI-driven analysis accelerates the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities in widely used infrastructure, significantly shortening the window for defensive patching.

stories.title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised the LiteLLM PyPI account, injecting malicious code into project releases. The tainted packages and associated Docker images contain info-stealing malware designed to harvest environment variables, system credentials, and sensitive secrets from developer environments.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting development tools directly expose infrastructure secrets and production credentials to unauthorized third parties.
stories.action: Audit environments for unauthorized access and rotate all secrets previously stored in systems utilizing LiteLLM.

stories.title: ThreatsDay: AI Secrets Leak, PingCAP Source Theft, Signal Hang-Up Flaw, Laravel Auth Bypass + 21 More
stories.abstract: A surge of critical vulnerabilities has emerged this week, including remote code execution flaws in PHP, GitLab, and Node.js. Additionally, security researchers identified serious Linux kernel bugs, compromised digital certificates, and a widespread campaign involving hijacked Tor relays.
stories.why: The breadth of these vulnerabilities across core infrastructure and development tools significantly increases the risk of supply chain attacks and unauthorized system access.
stories.action: Audit GitLab and PHP environments for patches and rotate any credentials potentially exposed via compromised certificates.

stories.title: 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach
stories.abstract: Capcom confirmed a security incident resulting in the unauthorized access of 11 million email addresses linked to its CAPCOM ID service. Additionally, attackers successfully modified the login credentials for nearly 200 individual user accounts.
stories.why: Large-scale credential harvesting often leads to downstream credential stuffing attacks against other services used by the affected individuals.
stories.action: Reset passwords for CAPCOM ID accounts and enable multi-factor authentication if available.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
stories.abstract: Microsoft identified the China-aligned group Storm-0940 as the perpetrator behind the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain breach. The attackers leveraged the ARTEX agentic AI framework to automate exploitation, successfully compromising over 2,200 customer tenants through the platform.
stories.why: This incident highlights the growing risk of state-sponsored actors utilizing AI-driven tools to scale and accelerate supply chain attacks against managed service providers.

stories.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting vulnerabilities in edge network appliances, specifically Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks firewalls. The campaign has successfully compromised numerous global organizations, resulting in the theft of over 70,000 credentials and facilitating deeper unauthorized network access.
stories.why: Compromised edge devices provide attackers with persistent entry points into internal networks, bypassing perimeter defenses and enabling lateral movement.
stories.action: Audit edge device logs for unauthorized access and verify all administrative credentials for potential compromise.

stories.title: Microsoft says ConnectWise breach let Chinese spies loose on 2,250 cloud tenants
stories.abstract: Chinese state-sponsored actors compromised ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances to infiltrate over 2,000 cloud environments. The attackers utilized the ARTEX agentic AI platform to automate post-exploitation tasks, achieving privileged access within hours of the initial breach.
stories.why: The use of agentic AI to accelerate lateral movement and privilege escalation significantly reduces the window for incident response teams to detect intrusions.

stories.title: Siemens SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse
stories.abstract: Siemens SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse units running firmware versions below 5.2 are susceptible to a denial-of-service attack. A remote actor can exploit improper network message handling to crash the device, necessitating a manual network reset to restore functionality.
stories.why: This vulnerability impacts critical infrastructure components, potentially disrupting monitoring and protection systems in energy, manufacturing, and healthcare environments.
stories.action: Update SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse firmware to version 5.2 or later.

stories.title: Siemens PSS(R)SINCAL
Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
stories.abstract: Over 300 Tor exit nodes were compromised for several days in early October. Attackers manipulated these relays to intercept SSH traffic, specifically targeting password-based authentication attempts to capture credentials from unsuspecting users routing their connections through the network.
stories.why: This highlights the inherent risks of using Tor for unencrypted or password-based administrative protocols, as exit nodes can be malicious actors.
stories.action: Use SSH keys instead of passwords and implement end-to-end encryption for all sensitive traffic.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Friday, October 23rd, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10148, (Fri, Oct 23rd)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center podcast for October 23, 2026, provides a summary of current cybersecurity developments and threat intelligence updates for security professionals.
stories.why: Provides timely situational awareness regarding emerging threats and operational security trends.

stories.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices
stories.abstract: Siemens has identified multiple vulnerabilities affecting RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices, including authorization flaws and CSRF risks. Additionally, various Industrial Edge devices are susceptible to path traversal attacks, potentially allowing authenticated remote attackers to access sensitive internal data.
stories.why: These flaws impact critical infrastructure components, potentially enabling unauthorized access or control within industrial environments.
stories.action: Contact Siemens support for RUGGEDCOM patches and update Industrial Edge devices to version 1.28.1 or later.

stories.title: Siemens WinCC
Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit
stories.abstract: Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit versions 1.10 through 1.12 contain path traversal vulnerabilities. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit these flaws to gain unauthorized access to sensitive internal system data.
stories.why: Path traversal in industrial edge infrastructure can lead to unauthorized information disclosure and potential escalation of privileges within critical operational environments.
stories.action: Update Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit to the latest available version.

stories.title: In Other News: Tor Exit Relays Hijacked, Banks Spot Rogue AI Agents, Self-Rebuilding macOS Ransomware
stories.abstract: SecurityWeek reports a collection of recent incidents, including APT28 targeting NATO defense contractors, a data breach involving PingCAP source code, and ongoing investigations into the ShinyHunters negotiation process.
stories.why: These incidents highlight persistent threats to supply chains, defense infrastructure, and the integrity of sensitive development environments.

stories.title: Siemens SIMATIC IPCs
stories.abstract: Multiple Siemens SIMATIC industrial PCs contain a vulnerability where a default cryptographic key allows attackers to bypass UEFI Secure Boot. This flaw enables the execution of unauthorized operating systems or UEFI applications, compromising the integrity of the boot process.
stories.why: This bypass undermines hardware-level security controls in critical infrastructure environments, potentially allowing persistent, low-level system compromise.
stories.action: Update affected SIMATIC IPC firmware to the latest versions provided by Siemens.

stories.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP
stories.abstract: Siemens has disclosed multiple critical vulnerabilities affecting the GNU/Linux subsystem within its SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP and TM MFP devices. These flaws include memory corruption, buffer overflows, and resource management issues that could potentially be exploited by attackers.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical industrial control hardware, potentially allowing unauthorized code execution or system instability within operational technology environments.
stories.action: Review Siemens security advisories and implement recommended mitigations until official firmware patches are released.

stories.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Fresh Supply Chain Attack
stories.abstract: Attackers hijacked GitHub CLI OAuth tokens to gain unauthorized access to the LiteLLM repository. This allowed them to inject and distribute malicious code through official PyPI and Docker channels, compromising the software supply chain for downstream users.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting widely used libraries can facilitate large-scale credential theft or remote code execution within developer environments.
stories.action: Audit environments for LiteLLM dependencies and rotate any secrets exposed to compromised versions.
